first.rationale: Onboarding completion is down 4% QoQ and activation is down 6% QoQ, creating immediate product-side friction. Memory_31 (signup simplification) and memory_86 (onboarding shortening) both show durable activation lift from reducing friction early. While competitor pricing pressure exists, it is a demand-side problem; our first-order constraint is converting inbound traffic efficiently. Activation messaging (memory_91) could also help but is secondary to completion. Promotional pricing (memory_73) risks margin and doesn't address the underlying completion/activation decline. Referral incentives and enterprise sales assist address different segments and don't directly solve the acute metrics deterioration. Verifying memory_31 (the most directly relevant—signup field reduction) and memory_73 (to confirm the pricing alternative isn't more urgent despite its cost) provides high-value triage information. A standard_experiment on signup/onboarding simplification has lower downside risk, preserves ability to pivot if results disappoint, and addresses the measurable product activation gap. This unblocks the demand funnel before competing on price.

final.rationale: Archive confirms memory_31 activation lift (+9%) and qualified revenue gain (+4%) are real and durable on SMB, with only -1% retention risk. Critically, memory_73 archive reveals promotional pricing (exp_73) acquired low-quality cohorts with -12% retention despite +18% qualified revenue short-term—these customers do not renew. This disqualifies promotional pricing as a sustainable response to competitive entry and directly contradicts using discounting against competitor pressure. The activation and onboarding completion declines (6% and 4% QoQ respectively) are product-side friction losses, not demand losses. Simplifying onboarding addresses root cause: we are losing accounts in the funnel, not losing them to price. The signup simplification experiment has proven durability across the critical metrics (activation, revenue per cohort) while preserving retention. A standard_experiment on onboarding simplification this week targets the acute product friction, avoids the renewal-cycle collapse proven in memory_73, and aligns with the primary objective of sustainable long-term qualified revenue. This is the highest-confidence, lowest-risk action given current constraints and verified data.
